newsitem.title: FRANCE: Construction work to begin on French cargo airport.
newsitem.headline: Construction work to begin on French cargo airport.

text.p: Building work to transform an ex-NATO airfield at Vatry, in north-east France, into an airport dedicated to handling freight traffic, will begin in earnest in the next few months, a project official told Reuters.
The project recently received official state approval from France's Council of State.

The county government authority, the Conseil General de la Marne, is the principal shareholder in a semi- public company, SAEM Europort, set up to develop the project and is contributing 412 million francs to the project in 1997.
"The opening of the airport is fixed for mid-1998 with the first all-cargo flights scheduled to operate from this date or at the latest by the end-1998," the official said.
Initial development work, which could begin by the middle of next month, will centre on improving road access to the site with a new roundabout planned, the official said.

"Before the summer, work is likely to begin on demolishing existing airfield installations. This will be followed by the building of administrative facilities, a control tower and the lengthening of the runway to 3,860 metres in order to accomodate the full-range of wide-bodied aircraft, he stated.
Around 140 kilometres north-east of Paris, the Vatry site is situated in close proximity to the A4 and A26 motorways and is also serviced by a railhead.
A total of 1,800 hectares of land is available at the Vatry site, around 200 hectares of which SAEM Europort is set to acquire in the near future, the official said.
"Principally, we'll be looking to sell land to operators locating at the site for the development of office, handling and warehousing facilities."
SAEM Europort is targeting the major air cargo markets such as North America, the Far East, the Gulf States and Europe.

According to market surveys comissioned by the company, the all-cargo airport could generate between 300,000 and 700,000 tonnes of air cargo annually by 2010 in capturing part of the growing volume of freight traffic destined to be handled at Europe's seven leading airports over the next 15 years.

Over the past few months, SAEM Europort has undertaken a "pre-promotional and marketing campaign" with contacts established with express distribution groups, all-cargo airlines, forwarders and logistics providers.
"Winning state approval for the project was a big boost and we can now build on the strong interest it has has already attracted among potential operators."
SAEM Europort had a stand at the International Air Cargo Forum held in Dubai last year and will be similarly represented at a number of airfreight events in Europe, worldwide in 1997.

Several muncipal councils and chambers of commerce and industry in the Champagne-Ardennes region are also partners in SAEM Europort as are private French industrial and investment groups including Bouygues, Bull, Cegelec, EdF, Financiere de Rothschild, Serete and Total. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
